rule.dip_definition: 1-day <= -drop_1d OR 5-day <= -drop_5d OR close >= drawdown_20d below its 20-day high; needs 252 bars of history

variants.V2_no_knife: dip rule, falling knives removed (price only)
variants.V3_quality_indicative: dip rule with today's quality score >= min (INDICATIVE: today's fundamentals leak into the past)

universe.bias: current constituents only: survivorship bias; delisted names are missing

entry: next close after the signal bar (the signal uses data up to and including the signal bar's close)
exit: h trading bars after entry; h in horizons

costs.note: subtracted from event returns; baselines are compared before costs on both sides

split.purge: in-sample events whose exit is after the cutoff are dropped

baselines: own: same stock, non-dip days with a computable signal, same period
index: ^GSPC (US) / ^STOXX (Europe+Nordic), same dates, not FX adjusted
peers: mean of all other universe stocks the same signal date
date-shift placebo: all events moved by one common random lag of 70-400 bars, paired comparison (keeps clusters)
independent placebo: same stock, random non-dip day of the same year (ignores clustering; reference only)
revisions_after_first_look: Run 1 (spec 90205cfc6da3a007) was a full run that included the out-of-sample primary cell, so the freeze is 'before the first run', not before anyone saw a number. Its spec file was overwritten by the next run (only the hash survives in trials.csv); specs are now archived by hash.

Placebo: the independent same-stock same-year draw ignores that events share dates and gave p = 0.002 beside an interval that included zero. A date-shift placebo that moves all events by one common lag replaced it; the independent one stays in results.csv as 'placebo_*'. This lowered significance.
Baseline and placebo days must have a computable signal (252 bars of history); before, a stock's first year counted as 'non-dip'. No predictable direction; the primary cell did not move.
92 zero-volume bars were removed before the run (91 exchange-holiday placeholders and one corrupt price). They were all in sample.
Later runs with the same analysis (same numbers) only changed report charts and wording, so trials.csv shows several runs per spec.

Found by the independent review and NOT acted on in the numbers: one more bad price (KNEBV.HE 2025-07-29) creates one false out-of-sample event; removing it moves the primary excess from +0.2660% to +0.2667%.

stress.definition: regional index closes >= stress_drawdown below its trailing stress_window-bar high

primary_hypothesis: For the price-only dip rule (V1), after the cooldown, the mean 21-trading-day forward return (entry at the next close), minus the same stock's mean 21-day return on its non-dip days in the same period, is greater than zero in the out-of-sample period (the last 40% of trading dates), all regions pooled, before costs. It counts as supported only if the 90% month-clustered bootstrap interval excludes zero. Every other cell in the report is descriptive.
sample_notes: events touching a >40% one-day move stay in the main numbers and are also reported without them
